key_insight: Fed-GRPO adapts GRPO to federated learning by using reward statistics as zero-cost signals to coordinate aggregation, calibration, and communication without sharing raw data.
engineering_relevance: It offers a privacy-preserving training recipe for distributed LLM reasoning systems that can reduce bandwidth dramatically while staying close to centralized performance.
method: Signal-weighted aggregation uses each client’s reward standard deviation to prioritize stronger learning signals.
Global reward calibration re-weights local objectives using the local-global reward gap to target weaknesses.
Adaptive sparse communication allocates bandwidth based on how informative each client update is.
evidence_signal: On mathematical reasoning benchmarks, the method outperforms other federated baselines, approaches centralized training, and achieves up to 32× lossless communication reduction and 621× compression under tight budgets.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on the quality and stability of reward signals, so noisy or highly non-iid client rewards may make calibration and update selection harder.
paper_title: Fed-GRPO: Reward-Signal-Driven Federated Group Relative Policy Optimization
